summary: Map placement data is real for only 51/98 gardens (CanonGraph ecosystem rows) and core-doc shelf data for 20/29 named gardens; at real launch most of the estate's positions/rings will be fallback or unscanned, undermining the map's #1 job (gestalt/spatial memory) and the trust needed to open it daily.

3 of 4 map lenses (allocation, dependencies, neglect) are seasonal-reshaping concerns per autarch-03 (rare, deliberate cadence) but are proposed as permanent daily-visible screen real estate beside the rail, in tension with autarch-01's 'quiet unless attention-worthy' doctrine; likely demo-ware for daily use.

The Mycroft composer in the rail duplicates BB's own thread-based interaction (bbDev/bbOps coordinator threads already surface as rail items); doc doesn't justify a third chat surface, and the composer's flagship bootstrap-from-rail flow auto-dispatches an agent in the prototype despite ruling 8 gating dispatch behind an unresolved one-coordinator claim (Open Q5).

Rail renders agent-authored proposal/question text via innerHTML together with embedded action buttons (data-approve/data-bootok) in the same string — a compromised or careless proposal can relabel/hide the real approve/override control, tricking mk into approving something else (autarch-map-rail-v2.html:280,252).

Answer, Approve (dispatch), Authorise (bd init), Approve bootstrap (creates private repo + wires CI), and Override & approve (bypasses an upstream blocker) all share one undifferentiated button pattern with no audit trail recorded beyond an ephemeral toast — click cost does not scale with blast radius.

T1 approval-driven dispatch is scheduled before the one-coordinator claim mechanism exists (decision 8), while bbDev/bbOps coordinator threads already run outside Mycroft's suggestion flow — double-dispatch risk is present at T1, not only at autonomous tiers.

Autarch holds no state is already false (preferences.json, display.go yaml prefs, in-process escalate.DecisionQueue) and the brainstorm adds more state (pins, seen-glow, composer history) without assigning an owner per item

Mycroft coordinates agents as BB threads is a rewrite of the dispatch substrate: current Mycroft (spawn/spawner.go, patrol/source.go) is 100% tmux-session based with zero BB integration, and this isn't named as scope
GraphSource, which the map's placement is supposed to read through, is only a plan (docs/plans/2026-09-03-layer-view-plan.md) — internal/door/graph.go and layers.go don't exist yet
Mycroft proposals create reinforcing feedback loop, amplifying escalation load on the rail
New-project bootstrap has no estate-size valve, risking unbounded sprawl and layered complexity
Neglect signal conflates peaceful steady-state with abandonment; slow-layer gardens become invisible
